messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: reserved-dedicated-pool-42 saturation > 95% (queue growth) — paging oncall (alice_oncall) :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: saw the page, jumping in. queue length spiking for resv-pool-42, lots of stalled sessions. any customer-facing errors?

ben_sre: yes, throttles showing in the gateway logs for enterprise tenants: `HTTP 429` spikes around 17:03 UTC. metrics: pool_util=99%, queue=~680 pending requests, p95 latency climbing.

carla_runtime: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with `scale limit reached` and `allocation timeout`. looks like node requests are queuing at infra layer.

frank_infra: infra side: GPU club has free hosts but they're all reserved to other pools, cannot reassign due to capacity reservations + placement constraints. autoscaler tries to create instances but hits quota for `dedicated-gpus` in region us-west-2.

alice_oncall: tagging product & cs. @dave_prodops @eve_cs — customers on reserved tiers might see failed allocations. please stand by for impact list.

dave_prodops: on it. pulling tenant map for pool-42. affected tenants: BrightLeaf (enterprise-2), KoiHealth, NovaHealth (all reserved). KoiHealth running heavy batch inference right now (scheduled jobs).

eve_cs: pinged BrightLeaf and NovaHealth — BrightLeaf is seeing request errors surfaced to their app, NovaHealth reported slow inference in monitoring. Sent initial advisory: "we're investigating, might see degraded throughput."

ben_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) evict noisy sessions (non-critical long-running jobs) from pool-42 2) temporarily relax reservation constraints to borrow GPUs from pool-43 3) fail open to hosted fallback for enterprise tenants (risk: data path/contract) 4) request emergency quota bump (slow).

carla_runtime: we can script an eviction for idle sessions with `reservation eviction` tag, but must coordinate with CS for tenant impact. I can push a patch to autoscaler to ignore quotas and mark nodes as `transient` but that's a risky manual override.

frank_infra: quota request to cloud provider will take ~20-30m if approved; not reliable for immediate. borrowing from pool-43 is quickest if they have slack. checking pool-43 now.

frank_infra: pool-43 has ~6 available GPUs idle. If we lift strict reservation binding, we can move 4 GPUs into pool-42 within ~2 minutes. We need approval to change reservation policy temporarily.

alice_oncall: do it. approve temporary reservation loosen. coordinating with CS: @eve_cs tell customers we may shift capacity and that we expect ~90s to see effect.

eve_cs: messaging to customers sent: "We are temporarily shifting capacity to restore throughput. You may see transient session restarts. We will update within 15 minutes."

carla_runtime: executing reservation-relax patch now: `./tools/reservation-relax --from pool-43 --to pool-42 --gpus 4 --transient`

carla_runtime: patch applied. autoscaler detected new nodes, starting model shards placement...

ben_sre: seeing queue drop from ~680 -> 210 in the last 40s. p95 latency improving. throttles reduced but not gone.

alice_oncall: nice. keep an eye for noisy tenant continuation. we should identify origin sessions.

carla_runtime: running analysis to find highest token-rate sessions. query: `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM active_streams WHERE pool='pool-42' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum(tokens) DESC LIMIT 10;`

carla_runtime: top offender is `koihealth-batch` — long-running multi-hour batch jobs that are saturating KV cache and preventing efficient shard placement.

dave_prodops: we need to throttle or reschedule koihealth batches. @eve_cs coord to get them to pause non-urgent runs.

eve_cs: on the phone with KoiHealth ops now. their window is flexible; they agreed to pause one heavy pipeline and move jobs to their off-peak window. will confirm when paused.

frank_infra: with the 4 GPUs moved we still see 75% utiliz and queue ~40. good but still some risk. request to also evict idle and retryable sessions to get below 50%.

ben_sre: running eviction: `evict --pool pool-42 --filter \"txn_time>2h OR label=idle\" --dry-run` -> returns ~120 sessions. starting actual eviction with `--grace 30s`.

carla_runtime: eviction triggered. monitoring effects... queue dropping to 12, p95 back to normal. no new 429s for the last 2 minutes.

alice_oncall: monitoring for recurrence. set incident status: mitigation in progress. assigning follow-ups: frank to handle quota request, carla to add autoscaler guardrail, ben to run post-incident analysis, dave/eve to handle customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427 (priority P1) — dedicated-pool-capacity-exhaustion; responders: alice_oncall, ben_sre, carla_runtime, frank_infra, dave_prodops, eve_cs.

frank_infra: quota request submitted to cloud provider—marked urgent. case #CL-98323. asked for temporary bump + ability to create transient nodes.

carla_runtime: root cause notes so far: heavy batch jobs + strict reservation bindings prevented autoscaler from pulling neighboring slack; autoscaler hit `scale limit` path because of quota and placement constraints. We'll propose a policy tweak: allow controlled borrowing with telemetry-based rollback.

ben_sre: saving logs and heatmaps. I'll export sample traces and token-rate histograms for postmortem. also patching alert thresholds to trigger earlier at 70% sustained with queue growth.

dave_prodops: for remediation roadmap: 1) implement transient-borrow policy 2) add tenant-level batch shaping (limit long-running offline batches in busy windows) 3) make reservation-relax an automated playbook with CS-approved impact messaging 4) add autoscaler metrics on `quota-blocked` events.

eve_cs: customers updated: BrightLeaf & NovaHealth acknowledged; KoiHealth paused jobs. they'll want an RCA and SLAs check. Preparing customer-facing timeline and mitigation notes.

gina_support: catching up — any escalation pages from enterprise before we relaxed reservation? we should attach tickets to INC-2026-0427.

alice_oncall: yes, two support tickets created earlier. I'll link them in the incident and follow up with handoff doc.

carla_runtime: quick note — autoscaler code path fix: add fallback to attempt `transient_allocate` when `quota error` seen, with a strict kill-switch. I will prototype and run canary tomorrow morning.

ben_sre: marking incident as 'mitigated' at 4575010289. queue stable < 10, pool_util ~52%.

alice_oncall: thanks team. handoff to daytime oncall (ben_sre) for investigation and postmortem. I'll compile timeline and initial actions, then close once RCA and customer comms ready.

ben_sre: will take over. next steps: collect logs, confirm quota result, file postmortem with suggested SLAs for reservation borrowing.

frank_infra: cloud provider approved temporary bump 20 GPUs in us-west-2, case closed. we'll gradually roll back transient borrow in safe window.

eve_cs: customers want ETA for permanent fix — giving them our remediation plan and target: policy + autoscaler guardrail in 2 weeks, postmortem within 3 business days.

alice_oncall: closing page. final note: we should run chaos tests for reserved-pool borrowing scenarios to avoid surprises. :white_check_mark:

ben_sre: acknowledged. creating follow-up tasks in INC-2026-0427 and assigning owners.

carla_runtime: adding script snippets and notes to the incident doc for future automation.

alice_oncall: good work everyone.
